MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MARCH 4, 2024

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR MEDAWAR at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

VICE CHAIR OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Medawar, Olson, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli,
  Schachter, Yoo,

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, FEBRUARY 5, 2024

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 5,
  2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER OLSON, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240055; ADDRESS: 6 BRANDING IRON LANE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: ELIZALDE BUENDIA;
  DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-240066)
  and a Variance to allow an 81 square foot addition to project beyond the forwardmost
  building line (V-240056) and a Minor Deviation to allow a decrease in the front yard of not
  more than ten percent (MD-240057).

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation for Planning Application PA-240055 summarizing
the staff report. In 2019, the owners received planning approval for a remodel and addition;
however, the project was not realized due to the pandemic. The property owners reapplied for the
remodel and addition in 2023, and that previously approved project is currently under
construction. The proposed project includes an 81 SF addition, 156 SF covered porch, and 53 SF
open porch.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission that the
Planning Commission; 1. Open the Public Hearing; 2. Take public testimony; 3. Discuss the
issues; 4. Close the Public Hearing; and 5. Adopt Resolution No. PA-240055, approving the
project.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MARCH 4, 2024
  1
 COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that this project is straightforward and commented
that the definition of the front yard setback and the inability to encroach due to the existing building
seems restrictive and asked if this is going to be proposed to be changed with the Zoning Code
update. Director Naughton agreed and stated that this will be addressed when staff presents items
for the residential districts.

In response to a question by CHAIR MEDAWAR, Director Naughton stated that the disadvantage
with expanding into the front yard of this residence was its unique siting in relation how the code
defines the front yard and it being setback more than 80 feet from the front property line.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. PA-240055, APPROVING THE PROJECT.

AYES: Medawar, Olson, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has adopted Resolution No. PA-240055,
a request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination and a Variance to allow an 81 square
foot addition and 156 SF porch cover to an existing single-family home that projects beyond the
forwardmost building line and a Minor Deviation to construct a porch cover that reduces the front
yard of not more than ten percent at property address 6 Branding Iron Lane. There is a 20-day
appeal period for any member of the public and the City Council by its own motion.

8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240028; ADDRESS: 12 CELESTE PLACE, ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: JOEL GUINTO, ALFRED DESIGN, INC.; A
  request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-240029) and approval of a
  Grading application (G-240030) for the demolition of existing retaining walls, construction
  of one replacement retaining wall and cut of a slope with a vertical height of five feet at its
  deepest point, all at the rear of the property.

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation for Planning Application PA-240055 summarizing
the staff report. The project includes demolition of the existing retaining walls and concrete steps
in the rear yard, construction a replacement retaining wall, and associated grading for these
improvements; the excavated material will be used to backfill the existing pool. The intention of
this replacement retaining wall is to address concerns with the wall since it appears to be
constructed without permits and to support rear yard improvements.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommend that the Planning Commission approve PA-
240028, subject to the conditions outlined in the staff report.

COMMISSIONER YOO inquired about any comments from the neighbors. Senior Planner Berry
stated that no comments were received for this project.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR inquired about the elimination of the pool and any details on how it will
filled in. Director Naughton stated that the contractor will need to follow specific guidelines outlined
in the Building Code for filling in the pool.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the plans have been reviewed by the building plan check
engineer. Director Naughton stated that applicants are not allowed to move forward with building
plan check until their project is approved by the Planning Commission. Some applicants may
choose to submit their plans at-risk, but this applicant did not choose to do this.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MARCH 4, 2024
  2
 VICE CHAIR OLSON stated that the grading application states that no heavy equipment will be
used to install the caissons and expressed concern with safety. Director Naughton stated that
detailed plans including an operational plan and safety measures will need to be submitted during
the Building and Safety review prior to permit issuance.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER
to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240028 WITH THE CONDITIONS
  OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

AYES: Medawar, Olson, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No.
PA-240028, a request for Neighborhood Compatibility Determination and approval of a Grading
Application for the demolition of retaining walls and construction of one replacement retaining wall
and cut of a slope with a vertical height of five feet at its steepest point at property address 12
Celeste Place. There is a 20-day appeal period for any member of the public and the City Council
by its own motion.

B.  2023 HOUSING ELEMENT AND GENERAL PLAN ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation on the Annual Progress Report (APR) for the
Housing Element and General Plan Update as mandated by Government Code 65400 and 65700.
An overview of the progress that staff have made during 2023 was provided.

Senior Planner Berry stated that the Housing Element APR is broken down by calendar year by
applications received and deemed complete; entitlement approvals; building permit issuance; and
certificate of occupancy. The city received applications for a total of eight accessory dwelling units
(ADU) and one 90-unit apartment building. The application for the 90-unit apartment building is
under review and requires discretionary approval by the Planning Commission and City Council;
and the ADUs were approved ministerially. Seven building permits were issued for new residential
development and included one single-family residence and six ADUs. Five certificate of
occupancies were issued for new ADUs.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission receive the City
of Rolling Hills Estates’ 2023 General Plan and Housing Element APRs, discuss the issues, and
recommend to the City Council that staff be directed to submit the respective APRs to OPR and
HCD by April 1, 2024.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if ADUs in the city are new construction or
conversions of existing space, like garage conversions. Director Naughton stated that most are
new detached ADUs and one garage conversion; the city has also seen barn conversions.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN, Director Naughton stated
that the City has not received any inquiries or applications related to SB9.

CHAIR MEDAWAR asked about staff’s expectations on applications for ADUs. Director Naughton
stated that staff anticipated more applications for ADUs especially with the development of the
City’s ADU Program, which provides free net zero plans to residents. Most ADU applicants want
their own custom designs.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the frequency of submitting these reports. Director
Naughton stated that the APR report is done once annually and there is an additional General
Planning survey midyear, with OPR; however, it is not required to be reviewed by the Planning
Commission and City Council.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that the
General Plan is for a 20-year period and the Housing Element is for an 8-year period from 2021-
2029. The city has made substantial compliance towards meeting the Regional Housing Need
Allocation (RHNA), predominantly through the ADUs and additional affordable levels will be met
with the 90-unit apartment building that is being proposed. The Office of Planning and Research
(OPR) does not generally provide feedback on the General Plan APR. Housing and Community

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MARCH 4, 2024
  3
 Development (HDC) will reply if they notice any errors in reporting and validation of data and staff
will work with them directly prior to submitting the final report.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS inquired about parking requirements for new ADUs. Director
Naughton stated that generally parking is not required for new ADUs; parking can be satisfied on-
site in the driveway and there is no longer a requirement for garage parking. The City also issues
annual parking permits limited to two permits per unit.

CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that there are two ADUs on his street and it can become problematic
and stated that the City should consider being more restrictive in issuing parking permits.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER YOO, Director Naughton stated that per State
Law the City cannot require covered parking for a new ADU.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked if SB9 applies to communities under an HOA. Director Naughton
stated that she is unsure whether it overrides CC&Rs.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that the city is proactive in resolving issues due to parking.

CHAIR MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  RECEIVE THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES’ 2023 GENERAL PLAN AND
  HOUSING ELEMENT APRS AND RECOMMEND TO THE CITY COUNCIL THAT STAFF
  BE DIRECTED TO SUBMIT THE RESPECTIVE APRS TO OPR AND HCD BY APRIL 1,
  2024.

AYES: Medawar, Olson, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS inquired about the update of the changes for the Commercial District.
Director Naughton stated that these will be presented at the next Planning Commission meeting.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS inquired about the “first-look” meetings for proposed projects.
Director Naughton explained that this is a way for development applicants to bring a preliminary
project to the City Council prior to submitting a formal application and plans for a project. This is
typical for larger projects. If the applicant chooses to continue, then the project will come before
the Planning Commission for review prior to going to City Council for final approval.

CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that with the rains there is erosion happening behind the buildings on
Silver Spur Road causing an overflow of mud in the parking lots. He and other tenants have fixed
issues themselves, but this may become an issue down the line. He stated that the city may need
to reach out to the building owners to prevent further issues.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, JANUARY 23, 2024

B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS - SPECIAL MEETING, JANUARY 23, 2024

CHAIR MEDAWAR, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM NO. 11A AND 11B

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR MEDAWAR adjourned the meeting at 7:54 p.m.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MARCH 4, 2024
  4
 The next Planning Commission meeting will be held on April 1, 2024 at 7:00 p.m.in the City Hall
Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Robert Medawar, Chair
